{{Short description|Differential operator in mathematics}}
{{Use dmy dates|date=July 2024}}
In [[mathematics]] &mdash; specifically, in the theory of [[partial differential equation]]s &mdash; a '''semi-elliptic operator''' is a [[partial differential operator]] satisfying a positivity condition slightly weaker than that of being an [[elliptic operator]]. Every elliptic operator is also semi-elliptic, and semi-elliptic operators share many of the nice properties of elliptic operators: for example, much of the same existence and uniqueness theory is applicable, and semi-elliptic [[Dirichlet problem]]s can be solved using [[Stochastic processes and boundary value problems|the methods of stochastic analysis]].

==Definition==
A second-order [[partial differential operator]] ''P'' defined on an [[open subset]] Ω of ''n''-[[dimension]]al [[Euclidean space]] '''R'''<sup>''n''</sup>, acting on suitable functions ''f'' by

:<math>P f(x) = \sum_{i, j = 1}^{n} a_{ij} (x) \frac{\partial^{2} f}{\partial x_{i} \, \partial x_{j}}(x) + \sum_{i = 1}^{n} b_{i} (x) \frac{\partial f}{\partial x_{i}} (x) + c(x) f(x),</math>

is said to be '''semi-elliptic''' if all the [[eigenvalues]] ''λ''<sub>''i''</sub>(''x''), 1&nbsp;≤&nbsp;''i''&nbsp;≤&nbsp;''n'', of the [[matrix (mathematics)|matrix]] ''a''(''x'')&nbsp;=&nbsp;(''a''<sub>''ij''</sub>(''x'')) are non-negative.  (By way of contrast, ''P'' is said to be elliptic if ''λ''<sub>''i''</sub>(''x'')&nbsp;&gt;&nbsp;0 for all ''x''&nbsp;∈&nbsp;Ω and 1&nbsp;≤&nbsp;''i''&nbsp;≤&nbsp;''n'', and uniformly elliptic if the eigenvalues are [[uniformly bounded]] away from zero, uniformly in ''i'' and ''x''.)  Equivalently, ''P'' is semi-elliptic if the matrix ''a''(''x'') is [[Definite bilinear form|positive semi-definite]] for each ''x''&nbsp;∈&nbsp;Ω.
